concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, the Hunger Clock is implemented through a system where the player's character has a hunger meter that depletes over time. If the player does not consume food periodically, they will become weak or eventually starve, which forces exploration to find food items.

In Broguece, the Hunger Clock is implemented through a system where the player's character must consume food items to maintain health and prevent negative status effects. If the player fails to find food within a certain time frame, they begin to suffer from hunger-related penalties, encouraging constant exploration of the game world.

In the game 'Crawl', the Hunger Clock is implemented through a hunger system where players must manage their food reserves to avoid starvation. As players explore the dungeon and engage in combat, they consume food, and if they run out, they gradually become weaker, forcing them to seek out sustenance to maintain their effectiveness and progress.

In 'cataclysm-bn', the Hunger Clock is implemented through a hunger mechanic where players must regularly consume food to maintain their character's health and stamina. If they fail to eat, their stats deteriorate over time, creating a sense of urgency that encourages exploration and resource management.

definition: A game mechanic that imposes a time pressure on the player through a hunger, food, or deterioration system. The player must find sustenance or resources periodically, preventing indefinite stalling and forcing exploration.
exclusion_criteria: Games without any time pressure mechanic
Optional food/healing that doesn't create pressure
Purely cosmetic hunger without gameplay consequences
inclusion_criteria: Player has a depleting resource (hunger, food, light, fuel)
Resource depletion causes negative effects or death
Creates time pressure preventing indefinite stalling
title: Hunger Clock
